title: A Soft and Living Heart
lyrics:
[Verse 1]
The people wandered far from home,
Their hearts grew hard as stone;
They would not listen, would not turn,
They tried it on their own.

[Chorus]
"I'll give you a new heart," He said,
"A soft and living heart;
I'll take away the heart of stone
And give you a new start."

[Verse 2]
The Lord spoke through Ezekiel,
"My Spirit I will send;
It helps you listen, helps you love,
And be a loving friend."

[Chorus]

[Verse 3]
Willow was mad all afternoon,
Her heart felt hard and cold;
Then something loosened, soft and warm,
She gave the boat to hold.

[Chorus]

[Verse 4]
So put your hand upon your heart
And feel it beating there;
"Please make my heart soft, kind, and new,"
He hears your little prayer.

[Chorus]
mood: Softening music. It begins a little stiff, like a tight fist: a few plain, even felt-piano chords with not much give, a steady pulse under the first verse. With each verse the chords open and loosen, the left hand starting to roll gently, like fingers uncurling from a stone into an open hand. Warm and unhurried by the last verse, the chorus the softest thing in the song, a hand resting on a chest.
